hook.line: Saying yes is easy. Saying yes with a catch is what Colombians do all day: a parent, a boss, a landlord, a friend with a car. Tomás needs a way to agree and set the condition in the same breath.
hook.es: Sí, pero que no se entere tu papá.
hook.en: Yes, but don't let your dad find out.

rule:
To say yes with a condition, put the condition right after:

*Sí, pero que* + what must (or must not) happen.
*Listo, siempre que* + the condition.
*Listo, mientras no* + what you don't want.

English says "as long as" or "but make sure". Spanish uses *que* and then a verb in its "wish" form: *se entere*, *estés*, *lleves*, *avises*. *-ar* verbs switch to *-e* endings, *-er* and *-ir* verbs to *-a*.

A plain *es* or *estás* after *siempre que* would sound like a fact, not a condition.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the present subjunctive after a condition.

readAndPick.es: Sí, pero que no se entere tu papá.
options: Yes, but your dad already found out.
Yes, but don't let your dad find out.
Yes, but you must tell your dad.

readAndPick.es: Listo, siempre que estés de vuelta antes de medianoche.
options: OK, as long as you're back before midnight.
OK, because you were back before midnight.
OK, but I'll be back before midnight.

readAndPick.es: Sí, pero que nadie toque la jaula de Simón.
options: Yes, but nobody touched Simón's cage.
Yes, but I'll touch Simón's cage.
Yes, but nobody is to touch Simón's cage.

readAndPick.es: Claro, siempre que lo laves después.
options: Sure, as long as I wash it afterwards.
Sure, as long as you wash it afterwards.
Sure, because you washed it afterwards.

readAndPick.es: Listo, mientras no me lleves al sitio de siempre.
options: OK, since you didn't take me to the usual place.
OK, while you take me to the usual place.
OK, as long as you don't take me to the usual place.

readAndPick.es: Sí, pero que me avises cuando llegues.
options: Yes, but let me know when you arrive.
Yes, but he lets me know when I arrive.
Yes, but I'll let you know when you arrive.

readAndPick.es: Está bien, siempre y cuando paguemos nosotros.
options: Fine, as long as they pay.
Fine, because we paid.
Fine, as long as we pay.

readAndPick.es: Sí, pero que no llegue tarde.
options: Yes, but he never arrives late.
Yes, but make sure he doesn't arrive late.
Yes, but he arrived late.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *se entere* or *se entera*. Yes, but don't let your dad find out. Sí, pero que no ___ tu papá. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Sí, pero que no se entere tu papá.
yourTurn.why: After *sí, pero que* the verb takes its "wish" ending: *se entere*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *estés* or *estás*. OK, as long as you're back before midnight (to a friend). Listo, siempre que ___ de vuelta antes de medianoche. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Listo, siempre que estés de vuelta antes de medianoche.
yourTurn.why: A condition after *siempre que* takes the wish ending: *estés*, not *estás*.

yourTurn.prompt: Yes, but nobody is to touch Simón's cage.
yourTurn.answer: Sí, pero que nadie toque la jaula de Simón.
yourTurn.why: *Toque* is the wish form of *tocar*: the *-ar* verb ends in *-e*.

yourTurn.prompt: Sure, as long as you wash it afterwards. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Claro, siempre que lo laves después.
accept: Claro, siempre y cuando lo laves después.

yourTurn.prompt: OK, as long as you don't take me to the usual place. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Listo, mientras no me lleves al sitio de siempre.
yourTurn.why: *Mientras no* also sets a condition, and the verb after it takes the wish ending: *lleves*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about we: Fine, as long as we pay.
yourTurn.answer: Está bien, siempre que paguemos nosotros.
accept: Está bien, siempre y cuando paguemos nosotros.
Está bien, siempre que nosotros paguemos.

yourTurn.prompt: Yes, but let me know when you arrive. (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: Sí, pero que me avises cuando llegues.
yourTurn.why: Both *avises* and *llegues* take the *tú* wish ending.

pitfalls.wrong: Sí, pero que no se entera tu papá.
pitfalls.right: Sí, pero que no se entere tu papá.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *sí, pero que* Spanish wants the wish ending (*entere*), not the plain *entera*.

pitfalls.wrong: Listo, siempre que estás de vuelta antes de medianoche.
pitfalls.right: Listo, siempre que estés de vuelta antes de medianoche.
pitfalls.why: A condition is not a fact yet, so the verb after *siempre que* takes *estés*.

pitfalls.wrong: Sí, pero no que se entere tu papá.
pitfalls.right: Sí, pero que no se entere tu papá.
pitfalls.why: The *que* comes first and *no* goes right before the verb.

personal: Think of someone who asks you for a favour. Say yes with one condition: *Sí, pero que…* or *Listo, siempre que…*
